mode: built-in image generation; style reference; no museum runtime changes

plates.title: DESCRIBE A JOURNEY

rows.label: 01  THE ARROW YOU CAN CARRY
rows.setup: Two small spheres, A off-white and B glossy black, on a broad tabletop with a red straight displacement arrow A to B. Student prepares to move the pair.
rows.reveal: Both endpoints have moved by exactly the same horizontal offset. Draw the old A/B pair as faint grey ghosts and the new solid A/B pair with an IDENTICAL red arrow: same length and direction. One rigid translated relation, not one endpoint stretched.

rows.label: 02  AIM WITHOUT CHANGING STRENGTH
rows.setup: A simple wall study with two parallel collinear-in-direction arrows, one short and one long, both angled up-right. Student compares them.
rows.reveal: Beside a small black point, two equal-length unit arrows now point in the same up-right direction, clearly labelled only '1' and '1'. They have equal length despite different initial displacements. No force, motion or shooter.

rows.label: 03  TWO MOVES, ONE ARRIVAL
rows.setup: Student places a black sphere at the beginning of a clear L-shaped floor route: short horizontal red arrow then perpendicular red arrow, head-to-tail, ending at one empty white plinth.
rows.reveal: Sphere rests on that end plinth. Preserve both red L legs and add a straight diagonal resultant from exactly the original start to exactly the same end. Triangle closure obvious, low wide view.
captions: First this way. Then that way.
One displacement reaches the same end.

plates.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create one finished portrait 2:3 museum comic plate, high detail and readable print typography. EXACTLY SIX PANELS arranged THREE ROWS by TWO COLUMNS. Each row is ONE idea: left SETUP, right REVEAL. Use the reference only for consistent protagonist, architecture, rendering and editorial lettering; all six compositions must be new, following the explicit scene instructions below.
STYLE: finely drawn cinematic editorial comic, convincing 3D bodies with delicate ink outlines, cream paper, black rectangular panel borders, warm off-white museum stone, quiet monumental spaces, simple pale rectangular plinths, beautifully observed soft moon/day light and contact shadows. Large condensed black serif headline, small uppercase numbering, clear serif caption strips. Palette mainly ivory, grey and black with protagonist's rust-red paisley shirt. The young adult student has short tousled brown hair, rolled sleeves, charcoal trousers, dark shoes; preserve this character across all panels. No helmet required. Glossy black sphere is the continuing point; cubes are off-white or charcoal. Minimal, legible geometry. Occasional unobtrusive wall title "ENDLESS MUSEUM" and underneath "always another room".
GRAMMAR: setup then a logically visible consequence. Arrows are explanatory overlays, not physical beams. Cyan = velocity or actual motion, amber = force, thin grey = prior state / prediction. Geometric vector diagrams use dark red. No arbitrary magical motion, explosions, broken joints or extra limbs. Make spatial relations precise enough to read visually; keep unimportant background details quiet. Display each idea number and short row title ONCE above its pair of panels. Limit wording to the exact headline, three row titles and specified short captions. No invented paragraphs. Distinct panels separated by gutters. Student and apparatus visible, not a collage of signs. One setup and one reveal per idea, not extra miniature subpanels. The pictures are proposal illustrations, not photographs or game screenshots.

SUBTITLE: "ENDLESS MUSEUM · IDEAS 01–03"
COLUMN HEADINGS: "SETUP" / "REVEAL"

LEFT PANEL: Two small spheres, A off-white and B glossy black, on a broad tabletop with a red straight displacement arrow A to B. Student prepares to move the pair.
Caption: "Two positions."
RIGHT PANEL: Both endpoints have moved by exactly the same horizontal offset. Draw the old A/B pair as faint grey ghosts and the new solid A/B pair with an IDENTICAL red arrow: same length and direction. One rigid translated relation, not one endpoint stretched.
Caption: "Move both. Keep the difference."
ROW 2 title: "02  AIM WITHOUT CHANGING STRENGTH".
LEFT PANEL: A simple wall study with two parallel collinear-in-direction arrows, one short and one long, both angled up-right. Student compares them.
Caption: "Different lengths."
RIGHT PANEL: Beside a small black point, two equal-length unit arrows now point in the same up-right direction, clearly labelled only '1' and '1'. They have equal length despite different initial displacements. No force, motion or shooter.
Caption: "The same unit direction."
ROW 3 title: "03  TWO MOVES, ONE ARRIVAL".
LEFT PANEL: Student places a black sphere at the beginning of a clear L-shaped floor route: short horizontal red arrow then perpendicular red arrow, head-to-tail, ending at one empty white plinth.
Caption: "First this way. Then that way."
RIGHT PANEL: Sphere rests on that end plinth. Preserve both red L legs and add a straight diagonal resultant from exactly the original start to exactly the same end. Triangle closure obvious, low wide view.
Caption: "One displacement reaches the same end."

plates.title: WHAT A RELATION KEEPS

rows.label: 04  SAME ARRIVAL, DIFFERENT JOURNEY
rows.setup: A black point at A faces a receiving plinth B. Two floor routes share exactly A and B: one direct, one long curved detour. Student considers both.
rows.reveal: The black point reaches B; the two different retained thin path traces remain between the SAME endpoints. Only one physical black point; old positions are faint ghosts. Emphasize unequal travelled lengths and equal endpoint displacement.

rows.label: 05  THE TARGET MOVED
rows.setup: A stationary glossy black sphere at A on a plinth, a receiving white cup at B on a sliding rail farther right. Red gap arrow between them.
rows.reveal: The cup alone has moved farther away and slightly up the diagonal rail, old cup grey ghost. Sphere A remains EXACTLY where it was. Red gap arrow updates to new B.

rows.label: 06  THE RAIL KEEPS ONLY PART
rows.setup: Front-on museum diagram made with real small sphere P above a long horizontal rail. A red diagonal displacement connects rail origin to P. A perpendicular grey line from P meets rail at Q, explicit right-angle square.
rows.reveal: Same geometry. Highlight red horizontal component origin-to-Q and perpendicular component Q-to-P. Both together reconstruct the original diagonal. A small white receiver sits precisely at Q. This is a projection diagram, not an object falling.
captions: Along the rail; away from it.

plates.title: WHEN A DESCRIPTION MEETS THE ROOM

rows.label: 07  A RECEIVER LOOKING ELSEWHERE
rows.setup: A pivoting white directional receiver with a faint cone of view; a near black sphere lies outside its cone and a farther one inside it. Student turns receiver.
rows.reveal: The farther sphere inside the cone is selected by a small light; the nearer sphere outside remains unselected. Preserve distances and positions. Selection tests facing direction, not nearest distance, and does not physically attract.
captions: Near does not mean in view.

rows.label: 08  WHERE YOU PUSH WILL MATTER
rows.setup: A geometric torque study: rigid lever arm from pivot O to tip; force arrow points along arm toward pivot. No motion. Small label 'diagram'.
rows.reveal: Same stationary lever. Force arrow now perpendicular to arm, lever arm r clear, curved dark-red TURN POSSIBILITY overlay around pivot and an out-of-plane axis symbol. This is a torque preview, not a real motor already rotating.
captions: Across the arm: a turning moment.

rows.label: 09  THE CUP ACROSS THE ROOM
rows.setup: Small catapult launching black point toward a white receiving cup across the gallery. Clear grey dotted parabola predicts arrival. A circular metal hoop intrudes into this path.
rows.reveal: Black point contacts the near rim of that hoop and cyan actual trail deflects away from the grey predicted parabola continuing toward cup. Single contact logically changes trajectory; no explosion, no shattered objects.

plates.title: A BODY KEEPS MOVING

rows.label: 10  YOUR BODY FOLLOWS THE ARC
rows.setup: The student stands on a pale launch pad, eyeing a broad raised receiving platform with safe lower floor beyond. Grey predicted jump arc.
rows.reveal: Student has landed on the receiving platform but forward cyan velocity carries them toward its far edge, arms naturally balancing; wide floor below makes recovery possible. Arrival does not automatically stop movement.

rows.label: 11  LET GO OF THE COMMAND
rows.setup: Student uses a hand control to push the glossy black point along a smooth lane. One amber force arrow forward, short cyan velocity arrow.
rows.reveal: Hand control released. No amber force arrow, same black point further along the lane with cyan velocity arrow. It coasts; no thruster exhaust after release.

rows.label: 12  SAME PUSH, DIFFERENT BODY
rows.setup: Two equal-size black spheres on parallel smooth lanes, one marked '1 kg', other '2 kg'. Identical amber force arrows, both from rest. Equal appearance except labels.
rows.reveal: After the same interval of the same applied force, 1 kg sphere is farther ahead with a cyan velocity arrow twice as long as 2 kg's. Keep equal radius and arrow force lengths. No claim about different gravity fall speed.
captions: The lighter body gains speed faster.

plates.title: THE ROOM JOINS THE MOTION

rows.label: 13  TWO POINTS CARRY YOU
rows.setup: Student holds one palm-sized glossy black sphere IN EACH HAND. Both emit narrow white thrust streams down and back. Student lifts up and forward, amber reaction arrow opposite exhaust.
rows.reveal: Same student airborne with BOTH spheres still in hands, triggers released. Exhaust completely gone. Cyan velocity continues forward, a downward amber gravity arrow. No instant hovering brake.

rows.label: 14  SAME FIELD, DIFFERENT JOURNEYS
rows.setup: Two identical parallel tabletop lanes with identical short uniform right-facing field arrows. Left lane label 'velocity', right 'acceleration'. Each has one glossy black point at start.
rows.reveal: Equal-time recorded position dots show evenly spaced positions in velocity lane and increasingly spaced positions in acceleration lane. One physical point at each lane end, earlier samples are ghost dots. Direction field same, interpretation different.

rows.label: 15  THE DRAIN BECOMES AN ORBIT
rows.setup: A shallow open circular off-white basin with one black sphere approaching center. Amber radial arrows inward. Student turns one tangential control.
rows.reveal: Added tangential component sends the black point circling around the center with a thin cyan curved trail. Inward arrows remain and instantaneous motion arrow is tangent. A possible circulation, not a guaranteed stable orbit; no cosmic black hole.

plates.title: WHAT RESISTS THE PLAN

rows.label: 16  THE TRAY REFUSES TO MOVE
rows.setup: Student pushing an off-white cube on a small tray across a rough patch toward a marked receiving bay. The tray is still; force arrow right and friction left.
rows.reveal: Tray now moves beyond the marked bay under continuing push, student reaching after it. Clean intact floor, thin ghost trace only. No stored-energy blast, no automatic spring. Emphasize a motion threshold and continued input.
captions: Then it moves beyond the mark.

rows.label: 17  THE ROOM TAKES SPEED AWAY
rows.setup: Identical black spheres launched equally on two parallel lanes labelled 'low drag' and 'high drag', equal initial cyan velocity arrows.
rows.reveal: Low-drag sphere travels farther, high-drag one less far with shorter cyan velocity. Amber resisting arrows point opposite rightward motion. Same mass and size, only drag differs.

rows.label: 18  SLIDE, ROLL, TIP
rows.setup: Two identical off-white cubes at tops of equal sloped ramps, one labelled 'rotation locked', other 'rotation free'. Same tilt, size and start.
rows.reveal: Locked cube slides remaining aligned as before. Free cube tips over an edge, visibly rotated mid-descent. Show different possible motions, no universal winner, no spherical rolling cube.

plates.title: RELEASE DOES NOT END THE STORY

rows.label: 19  THE PIPE RELEASE
rows.setup: Transparent curved tube, ending in a horizontal outlet pointing RIGHT. Black sphere inside near outlet; white cup below-left placed where someone imagines the curve will keep bending.
rows.reveal: Sphere exits initially straight RIGHT along the outlet tangent, then begins bending down under gravity. Cyan actual path to the right, thin grey mistaken continuation curls toward the cup below-left. Tube and cup stay fixed.
captions: Outside, it leaves on the tangent.

rows.label: 20  THE POINT RETURNS
rows.setup: Horizontal spring firmly fixed to left wall, black point attached at right end pulled right from marked rest position. Low-friction support, student releases.
rows.reveal: The same attached point passes leftward beyond the rest marker, spring now shorter/compressed. Cyan leftward motion arrow. Rest marker unchanged. This is the low-damping case, not every spring.
captions: Low damping: past the resting place.

rows.label: 21  A SECOND SPRING ANSWERS
rows.setup: Two black spheres on separate spring supports in a single horizontal line, each visibly tethered to a fixed frame. First sphere displaced toward second.
rows.reveal: First sphere contacts second, second moves and its own spring deflects while first changes direction/speed. Show clear single contact and intact anchored springs, no tangled ropes or fusing bodies.

rows.reveal: Gate reopened and cubes exit, but entry and exit are equally paced; the accumulated queue remains. Original backlog clearly visible with grey ghost marker. No infinite pile or self-cleaning disappearance.
